finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. An attacker can make the server request arbitrary URLs, including internal services, localhost, and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The full response body is copied back to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body returned via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) exposes the handler on :8080 with no authentication
target is read from the attacker-controlled query string
target is passed unchecked to http.Get; the default client also follows redirects
the upstream response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no authentication. The `allowed` map is only used by safeFetch, not fetch. The default http.Client follows redirects and has no custom dialer.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` unchecked to http.Get and main.go:22 copies the body back, the handler is registered unauthenticated at main.go:41, and the `allowed` host check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27), not fetch.
